key_insight: An optimized gradient boosting decision tree predicted friction stir-welded 7N01 aluminum joint strength with R² = 0.978 and mapped welding process windows targeting at least 90% joint efficiency.
engineering_relevance: The approach provides a quantitative basis for selecting welding parameters to achieve high-strength joints, with shoulder plunge depth helping refine the process window.
method: Predict ultimate tensile strength from rotational speed, welding speed, and shoulder plunge depth.
Compare baseline models, then apply gradient boosting and grid-search hyperparameter tuning.
Use SHAP to interpret parameter effects and identify high-strength process windows.
evidence_signal: Using 27 experimental samples and leave-one-out cross-validation, reported R² increased from 0.905 for a decision tree to 0.966 for gradient boosting and 0.978 after tuning.
watch_item: The small dataset and lack of reported independent validation warrant experimental confirmation before deploying the predicted process windows.
paper_title: Interpretable ensemble learning for tensile strength prediction and welding process window optimization of friction stir-welded 7N01 aluminum alloy
